quote: The whole account of the land of Judah and of the tribes is typical of the church in heaven. Let us read Joshua, the son of Nun, or the concluding portions of Ezekiel, and we shall see that the historical division of the land as related by the one finds a counterpart in the spiritual and heavenly promises of the other. What is the meaning of the seven and eight steps in the description of the temple? Or again, what significance attaches to the fact that in the Psalter, after being taught the mystic alphabet by the one hundred and eighteenth psalm we arrive by fifteen steps at the point where we can sing: "Behold, now bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord: you who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God." Why did two tribes and a half dwell on the other side of Jordan, a district abounding in cattle, while the remaining nine tribes and a half either…

Just as those who receive the law — which is a "shadow" of that true law — serve "the shadow and copy of the heavenly things," so those who divide the inheritance of the land in Judaea follow "the copy and shadow" of the heavenly division. The truth, therefore, was in the heavens, but the "shadow and copy" of the truth was on the earth. And so long as this "shadow" stood firm on the earth, there was an earthly Jerusalem, there was a temple, there was an altar, there was also a visible cult, there were high priests and priests, there stood also the cities and villages of Judaea and all these things which are now recited as described in this book. But when, at the coming of our Savior, God descending from the heavens, "the truth arose from the earth, and righteousness looked down from heaven," the "shadow and copies" fell. For Jerusalem fell, the temple fell, the altar was taken away, so…

But if, hearing that the inheritance of the perfect and the more eminent is called the Lord, you are ignorant and in doubt as to what that is which is designated under this name, hear that "the Lord is wisdom." He, therefore, to whom the Lord is said to be his inheritance, this one will take the inheritance of wisdom. The Lord is called "righteousness." He, therefore, whose inheritance is the Lord, this one will obtain the inheritance of righteousness. The Lord is "peace," the Lord is "redemption," the Lord is "salvation," in the Lord are "the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden." All these things he will receive in his inheritance, whose inheritance the Lord shall have been. Nevertheless, even these, to whom the "wisdom" of God and the "Word" of God and "truth" and "righteousness" is said to be their inheritance, meanwhile receive their dwelling together with those whose…

Let us learn from the law, which describes for us of necessity the division of the land, said to have been made first through Moses and secondly also through Jesus — not that we should keep both, but that, learning the meaning of each, we may hold only that one which is handed down by Jesus our Lord. Now that land which is "beyond the Jordan" Moses distributed; but this one, which is the "holy land" and the "good land," "Jesus and the princes of the tribes of Israel" distributed. You see, then, that when that true inheritance of the "holy land" begins to be distributed by the Savior, the "princes of the tribes" also of the true and spiritual "Israel" will be taken up. And whom do we suppose to be the "princes" of our tribes, or the princes of the church, if not the holy Apostles, to whom the Savior says: "you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel"? Yet…

However, he [the Lord] said they should not come to that land which they had refused, as a penalty for their unbelief; but their children and wives, who had not murmured, and who, owing to their sex and age, were guiltless, should receive the promised inheritance of that land. So the bodies of those of twenty years old and upwards fell in the desert. The punishment of the rest was put aside. But they who had gone up with Joshua, and had thought fit to dissuade the people, died without delay of a great plague. Joshua and Caleb entered the land of promise together with those who were innocent by reason of age or sex. The better part, therefore, preferred glory to safety; the worse part safety to virtue. But the divine judgment approved those who thought virtue was above what is useful, while it condemned those who preferred what seemed more in accordance with safety than with what is…
source_title: On the Duties of the Clergy 3.8.55-56

quote: And let us see who it is that first received an inheritance from Jesus. "Caleb," it says, "the son of Jephunneh." For he is the first to ask, and he asks with certain definite reasons and words, which are written down; and these words can also instruct us unto salvation. First of all, Caleb is interpreted as "heart." Who then is, as it were, a heart, if not the one who in all things devotes his effort to the understanding, who is said to be no other member of the body of the church than that which is more excellent in us, the heart — that is, one who conducts all things with reason and prudence, and so administers everything as though he were nothing other than a heart? Now Jephunneh, his father, is interpreted "conversion." This Caleb, then, is the son of conversion; and why, unless because, having been turned to God, he brings forth from himself such fruit that the heart begets a son?…

A brother asked John, 'What shall I do? A brother keeps coming and taking me away to help with the work which he is doing: but I am poor and ill, and too weak to do it. How can I obey God's commandment?' He answered him, 'Caleb the son of Jephunneh said to Joshua the son of Nun, "I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me with you to that country and now I am eighty-five. Then I was strong: and I am still just as capable of beginning and ending a battle" (cf. Josh. 14:6, 10–11). So go with him and see if you finish the work as well as you begin it. If you can't, sit in your cell and lament your sins. If they find you weeping when they come, they will not force you to go with them.'
source_title: The Desert Fathers, Sayings of the Early Christian Monks

quote: But let us also see his petition, which "Caleb, the son of Jephunneh," asked first from Jesus. "I ask of you," he says, "this mountain, as the Lord said in that day." The holy man seeks nothing lowly or base, nothing that lies in sunken valleys, but he seeks a lofty "mountain," and a "mountain" in which there are "great and fortified cities." For it is written: "there are the Anakim, cities great and fortified." And he was asking for these things because he knew how to wage war, as it is written: "the wise man occupied fortified cities and destroyed the stronghold in which the impious trusted." Do you suppose that, when Solomon said these things, he wished to teach us this — that "the wise man captured cities and destroyed strongholds" built of stones? Or does it rather indicate that the city and the walls are the dogmas of the impious and the syllogisms of the philosophers, by which…

Now Hebron is interpreted "conjunction" or "wedlock." By this can perhaps be shown that thing — that the double cave purchased by the patriarch Abraham is there, in which the marriages of the fathers and their remains lie, that is, Abraham with Sarah, Isaac with Rebecca, Jacob with Leah. Caleb, therefore, deserved to receive the remains of the fathers in his inheritance, without doubt because through the wisdom which was in him, by which he flourished both under Moses and under Jesus, he had understood the meaning of that very conjunction and had perceived what the cause was that with Abraham only Sarah lay there, and that neither Hagar nor Keturah deserved to be joined to him; or what the cause was that with Jacob only Leah seemed to lie, and neither Rachel, who had been more greatly beloved, nor any of the concubines had been united to him in the tomb. He himself, therefore, the…

Moses distributed the inheritance, and Jesus too distributed the inheritance. But it is not written in the distribution of Moses's inheritance that "the land rested from wars," whereas in the distribution of Jesus the very preface of the word begins thus: "and the land," it says, "rested from wars." If, then, you too wish to be made worthy to obtain an inheritance from Jesus, and to receive a portion from him, you must first bring all your wars to an end and stand fast in peace, so that of the land of your flesh also it may be said that "the land rested from wars."
